# ci/publish-token

Package publishing that a stolen token or cache can hijack.

npm publish (or pnpm, yarn, changesets, semantic-release) authenticated with NODE_AUTH_TOKEN or NPM_TOKEN from a secret instead of trusted publishing; id-token: write in a workflow that pull requests trigger; a dependency cache restored in the job that publishes.

- Default level: `warn`.
- Levels: warn. Publishing to GitHub Packages or another registry set with registry-url is not reported, because those registries do not accept npm trusted publishing.
- Looks at: each file in scope, on its own.
- References: [CWE-522](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/522.html), [CWE-829](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/829.html), OWASP A03:2025, <https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers>.

## Why it matters

A long-lived npm token in CI can be stolen by any code that runs in the job and used later from anywhere; trusted publishing issues a short-lived token per run instead. A cache restored before publishing can carry files written by another workflow run, which is how the May 2026 TanStack compromise published malware with valid provenance.

## Flagged

`.github/workflows/changesets.yml` (warn):

```yaml
cache: pnpm
```

`.github/workflows/changesets.yml` (warn):

```yaml
- uses: actions/cache@v4
```

`.github/workflows/changesets.yml` (warn):

```yaml
NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
```

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` (warn):

```yaml
id-token: write
```

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` (warn):

```yaml
echo "//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}" > ~/.npmrc
```

`.github/workflows/release.yml` (warn):

```yaml
cache: npm
```

`.github/workflows/release.yml` (warn):

```yaml
NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
```

## Not flagged

- `id-token: write` in `.github/workflows/changesets.yml`: push-only workflow
- `cache: pnpm` in `.github/workflows/changesets.yml`: this job does not publish
- `id-token: write` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: a test job (cloud login); forks get no OIDC token and nothing is published
- `id-token: write` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: this job runs only for tag pushes
- `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PACKAGES_TOKEN }}` in `.github/workflows/github-packages.yml`: GitHub Packages does not accept npm trusted publishing
- `id-token: write` in `.github/workflows/trusted.yml`: trusted publishing in a workflow that pull requests do not trigger
- `- run: npm publish` in `.github/workflows/trusted.yml`: trusted publishing needs no token

## How to fix

Publish with npm trusted publishing (OIDC, id-token: write) in a job that runs only on push, release, or workflow_dispatch, and restore no caches in that job.

## If the finding is wrong

Add a comment on the line above, in the comment syntax of the file, that says who decided and why:

```
ubon-ignore ci/publish-token: <who decided>: <evidence>
```

Or turn the rule off for the project in `ubon.json`: `"rules": { "ci/publish-token": "off" }`. See [configuration](../../config.md).
